title: The innkeeper (1203)
hookLine: Dominic stays up all night talking with an innkeeper who held other beliefs

cards: An inn in Toulouse, in the south of France. It's late. Two travelers from Spain come in off the road: a bishop named Diego, on an errand for his king, and a priest of his cathedral, a Castilian named Dominic.
They're tired. They want a bed. But Dominic gets talking with the man who runs the inn, and finds his host holds beliefs very different from his own.
He could nod politely and go upstairs. He doesn't. Today, the conversation that, by tradition, started an order.

teach.b: The story comes from Jordan of Saxony, who followed Dominic as head of his order and wrote down how it began. The innkeeper, Jordan says, belonged to the movement the Church called heresy and historians call the Cathars.

teach.h: A HOST WHO SAW THE WORLD ANOTHER WAY.
teach.b: They taught that the material world was not the good work of a good God, and they lived lives of hard self-denial that impressed their neighbors.
So Dominic, in Jordan's telling, spent the whole night with his host, talking earnestly and warmly.

teach.h: ONE TABLE, ONE NIGHT, UNTIL DAWN.
teach.b: Not shouting him down, not threatening: talking, listening, and talking again, until dawn. By morning, Jordan says, the man could not resist the wisdom and spirit of what he heard, and returned to the Catholic faith.
Notice what the story chooses to remember. Not a crowd, not a church council. One man, one table, one long night.
A line from the first letter of Peter fits. In the Douay-Rheims it asks believers to be "ready always to satisfy every one that asketh you a reason of that hope which is in you."
The next verse says how: with modesty and fear. Tradition says that night planted something in Dominic. Before it, he was a canon praying in his cathedral's choir.
After it, he wanted to spend his life explaining, patiently, to people who saw the world another way.

teach.h: READY ALWAYS TO SATISFY EVERY ONE THAT ASKETH.
teach.b: That's what his order would be called: the Preachers.

how: Dominicans tell the story of the innkeeper as the seed of their order, and Dominican friars and sisters still give much of their lives to study, preaching and long conversations with people who hold other views.

games.q: you're Dominic, tired from the road. you discover your host holds beliefs your Church calls heresy. what do you do?
o: nod politely and go up to bed.
stay up and talk with him, patiently, all night.
games.why: Dominic talked with him until dawn. Jordan of Saxony says the man returned to the faith, and the night set the shape of Dominic's life.

practice: Bring to mind someone who sees the world very differently from you, about faith, politics or how to live, and picture sitting across a table from them late at night, with nowhere to be.

Choose one question you'd ask, really wanting the answer, and notice what you'd have to set down to hear it: the need to win, the clock, the speech you've rehearsed; if you pray, pray for that person by name.

wordCard.voice: The innkeeper. The man who held other beliefs, and the night Dominic spent at his table, talking until dawn. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: all night talking. In the story, one patient night at one table is where the Preachers began. See you tomorrow.
